summary: In this project, we aimed to design a habitat where astronauts could live safely, comfortably, and sustainably. While designing our habitat, we also considered the challenges of Mars. To find solutions to these challenges, we designed a base consisting of three buildings. Our base includes a greenhouse, research areas, and spaces that meet people's daily needs. We also planned how energy, water, oxygen, and food needs could be met and how resources could be recycled. Through this project, we researched what would be needed to make life on Mars possible and designed a sustainable living environment for astronauts.
details:
What Is the Purpose of Our Project and How Does It Work?

Our project is a habitat designed to allow astronauts to live safely, comfortably, and sustainably on Mars. Our base consists of three buildings. We designed the central building as a greenhouse, research area, and workspace. We planned the two side buildings as areas where astronauts can stay, rest, exercise, and meet their daily needs.

We also planned the energy, water, oxygen, and food systems required for the base to operate. To meet its energy needs, we considered using nuclear energy and solar panels. For water, we considered extracting and purifying underground ice on Mars and recycling used water. We researched systems that could produce oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere and through the electrolysis of water. We also planned to grow plants in our greenhouse to produce food.

Benefits of Our Project and Its Intended Impact

The main purpose of this project is to show how human life could be possible on Mars. Since it would be difficult for astronauts to meet all their needs from Earth, we aimed to create an environment where they could use local resources as much as possible. By recycling resources, we aimed to use water and other supplies more efficiently. In this way, we designed a habitat that could contribute to carrying out longer missions on Mars.

Tools and Methods We Used to Develop Our Project

While preparing our project, we first used NASA's research about Mars and other scientific sources. We researched the environmental conditions of Mars, its water resources, and the systems needed to support life. Then, using the information we gathered, we created the design of our habitat and turned it into a physical model. We used PowerPoint to prepare our presentation and show our design.

The Creative Aspects of Our Project

One of the creative aspects of our project is that we designed three separate buildings connected to form a single habitat. By giving each building a different purpose, we separated research, plant growing, and daily living areas. Also, instead of designing a habitat suitable for only one location, we researched the regions of Arcadia Planitia, Utopia Planitia, Deuteronilus Mensae, and Elysium Planitia. By considering the different conditions in these regions, we tried to create a common habitat design that could be adapted to different locations.

Factors Our Team Considered

While creating our design, we first considered that Mars has environmental conditions very different from those on Earth. We focused on extreme cold, high radiation, the thin atmosphere, dust storms, and the difficulty of accessing water resources. In addition, we considered not only how astronauts could survive but also how they could comfortably maintain their daily lives. Meeting energy, water, oxygen, and food needs, recycling waste, protecting astronauts from radiation, and having backup systems for possible emergencies were the main factors we considered in our design.
